title: Pasta Making
strapline: Mix the dough, roll it thin, cut the ribbons — flour on your hands and a proper meal at the end.
intent: Children take part in a real, whole process — mixing, kneading, rolling, cutting and cooking — and see it through to eating.
Children build hand strength and control through kneading, rolling and cutting.
Children measure, count and compare — cupfuls of flour, how many eggs, long and short ribbons.
Children observe change: flour and egg become dough, dough becomes pasta, pasta softens in the pot.
Children learn about food from a real kitchen tradition and share what they've made.
implementation: Make simple pasta dough together — flour, egg (or water for allergies) — and let children feel it come together.
Give everyone real kneading, rolling and cutting to do, coaching the technique and standing back.
Measure honestly — count the cups of flour, crack and count the eggs, weigh the dough.
Talk through the change at each stage: sticky to smooth, thick to thin, hard to soft in the water.
Cut ribbons and shapes and compare — the longest strand, the shortest, whose is widest.
Cook a batch (adult-led at the pot) and eat it together, because the sharing is the point.
Bring in where pasta comes from and the many shapes and names it has across kitchens.
key_questions: What happened when we mixed the flour and egg together?
How many cups of flour did we count in?
Whose ribbon is the longest — how could we check?
How does the dough feel now compared to the start?
What changed when the pasta went into the hot water?

impact.text: Children take part in a whole cooking process and see it through to eating together.
Children knead, roll and cut, strengthening hands and refining control.
Children measure and count ingredients and compare long and short ribbons.
Children observe and talk about change as flour and egg become dough and then pasta.
Children learn about food from a real kitchen tradition and its many shapes.
Children notice being hungry and enjoy trying the food they've made.

enhancements: A simple pasta recipe with picture steps to follow.
Rolling pins, blunt cutters and a hand-cranked pasta machine (adult-supervised).
Measuring cups and scales for the flour and dough.
Trays and a drying rack for the fresh ribbons.
Real pasta of many shapes to sort, name and compare.
Aprons and a proper handwashing routine before cooking.
A table set for sharing the finished meal.

playing_exploring: Children plunge their hands into flour and dough and explore how it changes.
They test rolling it thinner and cutting it thicker to see what happens.
active_learning: Children stick with the kneading and rolling — real effort for a real meal.
The whole process, from flour to plate, gives the play a satisfying goal.
creating_thinking: Children predict what the dough will do and notice each change.
They solve the sticky-dough and torn-ribbon problems as they go.
